subject: Economics
chapter: Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues
central_question: How is employment in India measured and organised, and what do participation, sectoral change, informalisation and unemployment reveal about the quality of work?
in_scope_units: Introduction to the meaning and social importance of work.
Workers, employment, economic activity, GDP, GNP and the size and diversity of the workforce.
Worker-population ratio and differences by gender and rural–urban residence.
Self-employed, regular salaried employees and casual wage labourers.
Employment across primary, secondary and service sectors and rural–urban differences.
Growth and changing structure of employment, including jobless growth and casualisation.
Formal and informal sectors and the process of informalisation.
Meaning and forms of unemployment in rural and urban India.
Government employment-generation programmes and the chapter’s conclusion.
banned_topics: Rural banking and agricultural marketing, which belong to Rural Development.
Human capital institutions and education policy, which belong to Human Capital Formation.
Questionnaire design and sampling, which belong to Collection of Data.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only people receiving wages or salaries are workers.
known_pitfalls.correction: Self-employed persons and unpaid helpers in economic activities are also workers.

known_pitfalls.claim: A high worker-population ratio always means good-quality employment.
known_pitfalls.correction: It measures participation, not wages, security or working conditions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Self-employment always provides high income and independence.
known_pitfalls.correction: Many people are self-employed because other opportunities are unavailable, and earnings can be low.

known_pitfalls.claim: The formal sector includes every worker in a registered enterprise.
known_pitfalls.correction: Workers may be hired informally without security or benefits even in formal enterprises.

known_pitfalls.claim: Unemployment occurs only when a person does no work at all.
known_pitfalls.correction: Disguised and seasonal unemployment involve inadequate or unproductive employment.

recommended_example_progression: Use the Work These Out classification list to identify self-employed, regular salaried and casual workers.
Use Table 6.1 to interpret worker-population ratios by gender and residence.
Use Tables and Charts 6.1–6.3 to compare employment status and industrial sectors.
Use the chapter’s jobless-growth discussion to compare GDP and employment growth.
Use the end exercises on informalisation, unemployment and government programmes to build evaluative answers.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with an EXERCISES section covering worker concepts, participation, employment status, sectoral distribution, informalisation, unemployment and employment policy.
